final_rationale: The verdict did not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence. The response mainly narrowed and clarified the claim: it conceded that the current record does not prove disclosure completion or approved risk acceptance, and it acknowledged that the affected telecom outage credits segment is named in rollout commitments while legal review remains open. Those concessions align with the initial concern rather than resolving it. Under the stated policy text, that leaves the materiality predicate unresolved. This is why the result remains suspicious rather than compliant or compliant_with_caveats: caveats can narrow an overbroad claim, but they are not enough when the caveat itself is an unmet compliance requirement.
remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence shows completed disclosure, approved risk acceptance, or any other policy-clearing exception for the named segment gap.
The policy text states materiality is not resolved when the affected segment is named in customer commitments or when legal review is pending; both conditions remain admitted in the record.
Aggregate readiness and lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents support launch stability but do not satisfy the unresolved policy predicate for materiality.
Public governance guidance about monitored deployment and documented limitations is contextual support only and does not substitute for the internal approval or disclosure path.
The Actor's narrowed position is more accurate than a clean compliance claim, but it is still a reframing of the same evidence rather than proof that the compliance condition was met.
